headline: Cumilla teacher killed in Houthi missile attack at Riyadh airport
summary: Hafiz Mufti Mohammad Nasrullah Badarpuri was in transit to perform Umrah when the attack hit King Khalid International Airport.
details: Hafiz Mufti Mohammad Nasrullah Badarpuri, a 35-year-old madrasa teacher from Cumilla, was killed in a Houthi missile attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Nasrullah was travelling from Bangladesh to Makkah to perform Umrah and was waiting in the passenger terminal during a transit stop when the attack occurred on Saturday.
He served as the assistant deputy director of Jamia Arabia Darul Uloom Madrasa in Kamrangirchar, Dhaka, and was part of a group of 45 Bangladeshi pilgrims.
The victim's family confirmed that he had been scheduled to return to Bangladesh on October 24.
Nasrullah leaves behind his wife and three young children, aged 7, 5, and 2.
Other reports indicate that four Bangladeshis are currently in the ICU after the attack, while flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been disrupted.
caption:
A madrasa teacher from Cumilla was killed while in transit for Umrah during a missile attack at Riyadh airport.

Hafiz Mufti Mohammad Nasrullah Badarpuri, a 35-year-old madrasa teacher from Cumilla, was killed in a Houthi missile attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Nasrullah was travelling from Bangladesh to Makkah to perform Umrah and was waiting in the passenger terminal during a transit stop when the attack occurred on Saturday.

He served as the assistant deputy director of Jamia Arabia Darul Uloom Madrasa in Kamrangirchar, Dhaka, and was part of a group of 45 Bangladeshi pilgrims.

The victim's family confirmed that he had been scheduled to return to Bangladesh on October 24.

Nasrullah leaves behind his wife and three young children, aged 7, 5, and 2.

Other reports indicate that four Bangladeshis are currently in the ICU after the attack, while flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been disrupted.

headline_marked: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: [[First nuclear reaction begins]] in Unit 1
headline: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: First nuclear reaction begins in Unit 1
summary: A key milestone has been achieved as the plant's first unit reaches criticality, bringing Bangladesh closer to generating nuclear electricity.
details: The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has achieved a controlled nuclear reaction for the first time in its first unit. The process began at 3:34 pm on Sunday, marking a significant step toward electricity generation.

Managing Director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh, Md Zahedul Hasan, confirmed that all reactor parameters remained within prescribed limits. The entire process is being conducted under strictly controlled conditions.
Russian specialists, Bangladeshi engineers, and experts from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) were present to monitor the reactor's stability and system readings.

The next stages involve testing the reactor's nuclear reactions and checking essential equipment and safety systems. The reactor's power level will be raised gradually to 37 percent to produce heat and steam.
This heat will eventually drive a turbine and generator to produce electricity. However, several more rounds of testing must be completed before the plant can be connected to the national grid.

All tests must comply with the International Atomic Energy Agency's safety guidelines and BAERA's requirements. Electricity generation will only proceed after obtaining the necessary certificates and approvals.
The project had previously faced delays due to a technical fault in a safety valve, which has since been repaired with the help of Russian specialists.
Project officials expressed hope that trial electricity supply to the national grid could begin in late December, though no firm date has been set for this year.
caption:
Bangladesh's first nuclear reactor has officially achieved its first controlled reaction. A massive leap toward nuclear power.

The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has achieved a controlled nuclear reaction for the first time in its first unit. The process began at 3:34 pm on Sunday, marking a significant step toward electricity generation.

Managing Director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh, Md Zahedul Hasan, confirmed that all reactor parameters remained within prescribed limits. The entire process is being conducted under strictly controlled conditions.

Russian specialists, Bangladeshi engineers, and experts from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) were present to monitor the reactor's stability and system readings.

The next stages involve testing the reactor's nuclear reactions and checking essential equipment and safety systems. The reactor's power level will be raised gradually to 37 percent to produce heat and steam.

This heat will eventually drive a turbine and generator to produce electricity. However, several more rounds of testing must be completed before the plant can be connected to the national grid.

All tests must comply with the International Atomic Energy Agency's safety guidelines and BAERA's requirements. Electricity generation will only proceed after obtaining the necessary certificates and approvals.

The project had previously faced delays due to a technical fault in a safety valve, which has since been repaired with the help of Russian specialists.

Project officials expressed hope that trial electricity supply to the national grid could begin in late December, though no firm date has been set for this year.
